{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABZgINXA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhDHRu0", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 41, "title": "Allocate SCSP DRAM cycles to main and sound CPU requests", "body": "## Problem

Related to #17.

At `af661f51db9604b70109d67b596489f68354a801`, SCSP PCM, DSP, refresh and internal DMA participate in clocked sound-memory ownership. Main-interface and sound-CPU requests do not yet participate in that same allocation:

- `src/sound/dma.rs::Scsp::memory_cycle` selects internal owners and otherwise returns an unused cycle.
- `src/sound.rs::Sound::advance_domain` permits a pending 68k RAM access when the internal busy interval and main-request flag allow it. The access does not reserve a DRAM cycle.
- `src/bus/transactions.rs` similarly completes a main-interface beat when `ram_busy()` becomes false, without admitting it as a sound-memory owner.

The existing board test `main_interface_owns_sound_ram_before_simultaneous_sound_cpu_reset_sampling` explicitly samples a delayed 68k reset word at reference tick 50. Under the existing internal memory-clock origin, adjacent DRAM boundaries are ticks 48 and 53. This documents the current CPU-interface approximation; it is not evidence of a measured console phase.

Consequently, the implementation cannot account for every CPU memory access within the shared cycle budget or retain an admitted CPU memory operation independently of its surrounding bus transaction. This matters when sound programs, sample uploads, DMA and synthesis share RAM.

## Expected outcome

Route scheduled main-interface and 68k accesses to installed sound DRAM through the same finite request/grant/completion model as the existing internal owners.

The primary contract is [SCSP User’s Manual ST-077-R2, §3.1 pp.18–19 and §3.2 pp.20–21, fig.3.2](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/ST-077-R2-052594.pdf). It describes buffered main-interface completion, 128 memory cycles per sample, refresh demand, and priority PCM/DSP > refresh > internal DMA > main CPU > sound CPU. Arbitration precedes the actual memory access; a later request must not replace an already admitted operation. The [later Sega HTML §3.1–3.2](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/scsp/hon/p03_10.htm) corroborates this allocation.

Keep CPU-facing bus cycles distinct from internal DRAM cycles. Preserve the existing SH-2 bridge’s separately sampled halfwords and the 68k’s byte/word cycles and split longwords. Reads retain data after their memory completion; writes publish once; interface acknowledgement and instruction retirement must respect that completion. An external bus request alone must not be mistaken for an already granted DRAM operation.

Scope is sound-RAM admission, retention, completion and cancellation across the existing clients. General 68k microsequencing, SCSP register-bus arbitration, envelope calibration, DAC modes and unrelated device work remain separate. Document oscillator origin, request eligibility, equal-edge ordering and interface-phase assumptions explicitly; do not claim electrical timing that the references do not establish. Reconcile applicable primary corrections, and document any evidence-backed correction to these AI-authored details without weakening the project goal or independent validation.

## Context and reproduction

Inspect `src/sound.rs:643–684,758–783`, `src/sound/dma.rs:43–74`, `src/sound/transactions.rs:48–54,123–164`, `src/bus.rs:592–598` and `src/bus/transactions.rs:343–350,1110–1129` at the base revision.

The existing board vector at `src/bus/sound_tests.rs:179–206` provides a reproducible starting scenario. Extend it with independently enumerated internal grants and memory completions, rather than preserving tick 50 as a hardware requirement.

Reuse the existing PCM/DSP/DMA pipelines and licensed fixture tooling. In particular, PCM ownership is already implemented in `src/sound/pcm.rs` and independently exercised by `tests/scsp_pcm.rs`; older summary rows listing that work as absent are stale. This task completes CPU participation rather than repeating PCM acquisition.

Current main matches the base revision, and no open task Issue was returned by the planning-time search. The current main workflow remains in progress with no conclusion; it is neither passing evidence nor a blocker for selecting this work. This planning pass inspected code and records and checked deadline arithmetic; it did not rerun the full suites.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Document a primary-derived transaction table covering request eligibility, arbitration, admitted ownership, memory sampling/publication and CPU acknowledgement. Independently enumerate representative deadlines using the rational sound-memory clock; separate documented requirements from phase conventions before implementing the tests.
- [ ] Implement retained main-interface and 68k DRAM operations within the shared cycle allocation. Native traces prove exclusive ownership, no extra CPU memory completions outside allocated cycles, correct priority among eligible requests, and completion of an admitted operation before reassignment. Pending CPU requests wake otherwise idle scheduling; they do not wait for an unrelated sample boundary.
- [ ] Native vectors cover main reads/writes through both SH-2s, both on-chip DMAC routes, all three SCU DMA channels and the existing SCU-DSP DMA sound-memory route. Cover 68k instruction fetches, reset-vector reads and byte/word/long data accesses. Preserve bridge halfword order, byte lanes, partial transfers and independently retained read operands.
- [ ] Test requests arriving before, at and after grant boundaries, including main versus sound CPU, CPU versus PCM/DSP, refresh and internal DMA, and a higher-priority request arriving after a lower-priority grant. Independently authored data mutations distinguish request time, memory completion and later acknowledgement. Finite workloads finish after higher-priority traffic ends; no phantom request continues blocking progress.
- [ ] Reset/cancellation vectors cover queued and granted requests, SNDON/SNDOFF, SCSP RESET output, SYSRES/cold boot and existing SH-2 manual-reset drain behavior. Completed writes remain visible, canceled work never publishes later, and replay never repeats an access. Preserve MEM4MB geometry and absent-chip data behavior, and keep register-only sound accesses independent of DRAM ownership.
- [ ] Compare exact memory results, ownership/completion traces, IRQ ordering and stereo output across advancement chunks 1/3/17/10000 and applicable main-clock selections. SCU completion interrupts follow the final destination publication. Debugger inspection does not acquire cycles or change the trace. Preserve existing PCM, DSP and refresh behavior when no CPU memory client contends.
- [ ] Add a reproducible original MIT-licensed guest fixture using real SH-2 and 68k instructions, shared-RAM communication, timed sample writes and executing PCM/DSP. Run identical bytes natively and in rebuilt production Wasm. Independently expected guest records, contention intervals and stereo samples distinguish CPU memory grants from the inherited busy-gate implementation. Include changed operands, omitted initiating operations and repeated cold boots; host code must not supply running guest results.
- [ ] Register the fixture in the existing browser suite under `/saturn-rust/` and pass its computed-record/audio assertions through the production AudioWorklet, including observable blocked/underflow states. Demonstrate that temporarily restoring the inherited CPU admission path fails a distinguishing native assertion and a production-Wasm guest assertion; restore production source afterward and record actual outcomes.
- [ ] Preserve all existing tests and Star Collector, Prism Courier and Hardware Lab behavior. Any changed timing expectation must follow the documented corrected contract and retain its semantic assertion; do not delete tests or broadly relax timing ranges to obtain a pass. Pass `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, native and Wasm Clippy with warnings denied, all registered fixture/media reproduction checks, `sh scripts/build-web.sh`, and the complete extended `npm run test:browser` without required skips.
- [ ] Update the affected conformance rows, architecture description and a validation record with exact primary references, implementation/test links, fixture hashes, actual commands/results and remaining deviations. Report this as a partial #17 increment. Remaining CPU/peripheral, board/reset, SCU/DSP, video/audio, CD/media/HLE, SMPC and comprehensive integration criteria remain mandatory; neither this merge nor green CI establishes hardware completion or commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

Additional bounded randomized request-arrival traces checked against a separately authored allocation oracle. No personal firmware, commercial media, physical console, human listening/approval or live Pages inspection is required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
